alignments.note: Verb with auxiliary, discontinuous from its waw around the subject (rule 25).
No the is written for this article; the phrase's determiner answers to the present demonstrative (rules 15, 47).
Attributive article rendered by the relative that (rule 41).
Participle rendered by a light verb plus complement; head on the complement (rule 44).
Agreement article on the demonstrative, unrendered (rule 47).

The purpose לְ is left with no English word of its own: the ASV recasts the phrase as a coordinate clause and writes only a coordinator, which rule 14 says is not a word spent on the preposition's own relation (rules 52, 40). Competing reading: give the and to this לְ as the word written at the recast clause's left edge; rejected because rule 14 directs that a preposition whose relation the ASV has left unstated is unrepresented rather than a home for a coordinator.

No conjunction morpheme stands in this clause — the Hebrew writes לַצְבּוֹת with no waw — so the supplied coordinator answers to nothing and is its own added unit (rules 14, 30). The second such clause does write a waw, and there the and is that waw's.
Causative infinitive rendered make … to swell, headed on the complement verb (rule 44); the unit is discontinuous around the supplied possessive and the noun (rule 25).
No suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on בֶּטֶן, so the supplied thy answers to nothing (rule 18's closing sentence).
The second לְ has no English word of its own, the connective belonging to the waw written beside it (rule 40).
Causative infinitive rendered to fall away, headed on the verb, its phrasal particle joining it (rule 44).
Supplied possessive with no possessive morpheme on יָרֵךְ (rule 18).

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave the and of and make thy body to swell to the first purpose לְ. No waw stands in that clause, and rule 14's last sentence is explicit that a supplied coordinator is not to be folded into a neighbouring preposition — a preposition whose own relation the ASV has left unstated is unrepresented rather than a home for a coordinator. Rule 52's list of what a לְ may take is prepositions and complementizers, not coordinators. The and is now added and the לְ unrepresented, which also matches the coordinated second phrase, where the written waw takes its own and and the לְ is unrepresented.
The two supplied thy are added: בֶּטֶן and יָרֵךְ carry no possessive morpheme here (rule 18).
